For each `y`, compute texture index `p` using modulo wrapping on `height`/`width` [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the source notes: 'For each y, compute texture index p using modulo wrapping on height/width.' Furthermore, the provided C++ code snippet confirms this implementation: `int p = ((textures[wallTexture].height - (static_cast<int>(verticalStart) % textures[wallTexture].height) - 1) * 3 * textures[wallTexture].width + (static_cast<int>(horizontalStart) % textures[wallTexture].width) * 3);`. This code uses the modulo operator (`%`) on both height and width to calculate the texture index `p` within the loop iterating over `y`.
